I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little for price and weather. I only have myself at home, but I have 18.8 mu and a well, so I will keep the land mostly in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. Around Quzhou, if I cut fertilizer too hard and the stand turns weak, I cannot make that yield back later, so I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the crop go hungry. With my years in the field, and from seeing what nearby farmers do, I will keep wheat and maize on 15 mu and cotton on 3.8 mu. For wheat, I will use enough base fertilizer and give water at the key times, because wheat here responds well if I do not let it suffer in winter and at jointing. For maize, I will push nitrogen a bit because maize eats strongly after the wheat comes off. For cotton, I will not plant too much, because it takes more labor and more spraying, and I am alone. I will still keep some cotton because I know how to manage it and it gives me another income line if grain price is not good.
